VBO:0200283.summary: Cheerful, quick to learn and eager for work, the Cantabrian Water Dog may look composed at rest but becomes lively on the job. On Spain’s northern coast, it helped fishermen recover fallen fish, carry mooring lines between boats and shore, and watch tied-up vessels. Swimming and diving are central to its working tradition; its dense curly coat has an abundant undercoat.
VBO:0200283.shortDescription: A cheerful, eager water worker from Spain’s northern ports, with a tradition of retrieving fish and carrying mooring lines.

sources.title: Cantabrian Water Dog association — complete breed standard
sources.evidence: Personally read whole actual standard body: intelligent, active, cheerful, high learning capacity; calm-looking at rest and very active at work, willingness and enjoyment of water. Historical fishermen recovered fallen fish, guarded moored boats and carried lines between boats or shore; swimming/diving stated. Complete head/ear/body/limb/paw/white curly coat clauses and medium-set full tail hanging to hocks at rest with middle bend, no tailless dogs.

sources.title: Méndez and colleagues — Characterization of the Cantabric Water Dog (2011)
sources.evidence: Personally read complete actual article through references. Twenty-one Cantabrian samples and108 comparison samples/21microsatellites distinguish sampled population from nearby water dog breeds including published Spanish Water Dog. Introduces fishing work, declining boat use and numerous port companions as of2011,2009 regional register1216. Historical counts not current census; genetic analysis does not prove temperament, exclusive ancestry or every individual pedigree.
